properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency in the root yarn.lock: hash.js@1.1.7 ships SHA-1/SHA-224/SHA-256/SHA-384/SHA-512. Consumed transitively by @ethersproject/sha2@5.7.0 and @ethersproject/signing-key@5.7.0 (ethers v5, the wallet's Ethereum signing stack — apps/mobile pins @ethersproject/hash) and by elliptic itself. No direct first-party import of hash.js; the SHA primitives arrive in the shipped React Native bundle via ethers. SHA-1 in the family is deprecated; SHA-2 members are Grover-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency in the root yarn.lock: md5@2.2.1, pulled by @expo/rudder-sdk-node@1.1.1 — the Expo analytics SDK. Build-time tooling, not bundled into the shipped app. MD5 is collision-broken but the consumer uses it for non-security event hashing. The inventory keeps it because the toolchain ships the algorithm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency in the root yarn.lock: node-forge@1.3.1 provides RSA key transport, X.509, PKCS and TLS primitives. Pulled by @expo/cli (line 3572) and @expo/code-signing-certificates@0.0.5 (line 3602) — Expo build tooling that handles app code-signing certificates. No RSA call site in application source; the quantum-vulnerable RSA path ships in the build toolchain, where any cert/key material it touches is decided.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTION (supersedes earlier context): tweetnacl's Ed25519 arrives via @metamask/eth-sig-util@4.0.1 (yarn.lock:5574), which is pulled ONLY by hardhat@2.10.0 (yarn.lock:22125) — the Solidity dev framework declared as a devDependency at apps/mobile/package.json:207 and used for the local `hardhat node` e2e chain. Dev toolchain, NOT bundled into the shipped app. Ed25519 capability ships in the toolchain; quantum-vulnerable signature (migration ML-DSA-65) if tooling ever signs with it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA (secp256k1) via elliptic@6.5.4 — this is the wallet's core signing path: @ethersproject/signing-key@5.7.0 exact-pins elliptic 6.5.4 (yarn.lock:3396), and ethers v5 is the wallet's Ethereum transaction signer (apps/mobile pins @ethersproject/hash 5.6.1). Also reachable via create-ecdh@4.0.4 (crypto-browserify polyfill). Quantum-vulnerable signature at the heart of the product — every wallet transaction is secp256k1-ECDSA-signed today; migration target ML-DSA-65, and the ecosystem (EIP- post

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: build ships elliptic 6.5.4 (ECDH/ECDSA over secp256k1 etc.), a transitive dep of the Ethereum JS toolchain. Quantum-vulnerable key agreement capability; no first-party ECDH call site found in app code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTION (supersedes earlier context): X25519 key agreement capability arrives via tweetnacl@1.0.3 ← @metamask/eth-sig-util@4.0.1 ← hardhat@2.10.0 (devDependency, apps/mobile/package.json:207; yarn.lock:22125). Dev toolchain only, not bundled into the shipped app. (The wallet's actual runtime X25519 use is WalletConnect session crypto, reported separately as a finding.)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Live first-party password KDF for the wallet keyring: WebCrypto PBKDF2 (100,000 iterations, SHA-256, random 16-byte salt) deriving an AES-256-GCM key that encrypts keyring secrets (mnemonics/private keys at rest). 100k iterations is below OWASP's 600,000 recommendation for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256; the code TODO notes it should use Argon2 as Trail of Bits recommended for mobile.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unit tests of the production Argon2id KDF used for iOS iCloud cloud-backup encryption of wallet seed phrases: Argon2Swift, type .id, t=3, m=2^17 KiB (128 MiB), p=4, 32-byte SymmetricKey — RFC 9106-valid parameters tuned to ~1s per the security audit.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Authenticated encryption at rest for wallet data: Android cloud-backup EncryptionHelper.kt encrypt/decrypt (AES/GCM/NoPadding keyed by Argon2id-derived key, password+salt) and the WebCrypto AES-GCM-256 params completing the PBKDF2 keyring chain in crypto.ts. Symmetric AE — quantum-safe; the posture question is the KDF, not the cipher.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum transaction digest step before native signing: keccak256 (Ethereum's pre-standard SHA-3 padding variant) over the RLP-serialized unsigned transaction; the digest is then passed to Keyring.signTransactionHashForAddress (native ECDSA). Hashing is not quantum-urgent (Grover gives only square-root speedup).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES available via node-forge@1.3.1 (CBC/CTR/GCM modes) — transitive via @expo/cli and @expo/code-signing-certificates@0.0.5, build tooling. No node-forge AES call site in application source; the app's own AES-GCM use is native Kotlin/Swift (EncryptionHelper.kt / EncryptionHelper.swift, inventoried as separate objects). AES itself is quantum-safe against Grover at 256-bit keys.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTION (supersedes earlier context): SHA-256 via @noble/hashes@1.2.0 arrives through @scure/bip32@1.1.5 / @scure/bip39@1.1.1 / ethereum-cryptography@1.2.0, all pulled only by hardhat@2.10.0 (devDependency, apps/mobile/package.json:207; yarn.lock:22140). NOT the shipped wallet's mnemonic path — the production wallet derives keys natively in Rust ethers-rs. Dev toolchain only; SHA-256 is Grover-only regardless.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTION (supersedes earlier context): BLAKE3 via @noble/hashes@1.2.0 arrives through the @scure/bip32/bip39 → ethereum-cryptography@1.2.0 chain, pulled only by hardhat@2.10.0 (devDependency, apps/mobile/package.json:207). Dev toolchain only; BLAKE3 is quantum-safe (Grover square-root on preimages).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: REFINEMENT: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is exact-pinned by @ethersproject/json-wallets@5.7.0 (yarn.lock:3272), part of the ethers v5 tree that apps/mobile declares directly (ethers 5.7.2, apps/mobile/package.json:109). Bundled to the extent the app's Metro graph reaches ethers' JSON-keystore import path; the wallet's own keystore/backup crypto is native (Kotlin/Swift, inventoried separately). scrypt itself is memory-hard, quantum-resistant as a KDF.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes 1.2.0 provides SHA-3/Keccak/SHA-2/HKDF shipped in the JS bundle; keccak256 for Ethereum tx digests flows through this family via ethers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Android Keystore-backed at-rest key storage for the wallet: MasterKeys AES256_GCM master key plus EncryptedSharedPreferences AES256_SIV (keys) / AES256_GCM (values) protect the BIP39 mnemonics and derived xprv private keys that RnEthersRs stores. Strongest symmetric posture in the repo; the master key itself is held by the Android Keystore.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CORRECTION (supersedes earlier context): NaCl secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305) capability arrives via tweetnacl@1.0.3 ← @metamask/eth-sig-util@4.0.1 ← hardhat@2.10.0 (devDependency, apps/mobile/package.json:207; yarn.lock:22125/5574). Dev toolchain only. XSalsa20-Poly1305 itself is Grover/Shor-resistant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Correct CSPRNG choice for IV/nonce and salt generation in the Android cloud-backup encryption (generateSalt/generateNonce feeding AES-GCM + Argon2id). Not quantum-relevant.
